prompt: Young Carl Gauss was told to add every whole number from $1$ to $100$. He finished in seconds by pairing the ends. What is the sum?
hint: Pair the first with the last: $1 + 100$. Then $2 + 99$. Notice anything?

hints.text: Pair the first with the last: $1 + 100$. Then $2 + 99$. Notice anything?
Every pair adds to $101$, and $100$ numbers make $50$ pairs.

alternativeExplanations.title: Pair the ends, in pictures
steps: Write 1 to 100 in a row, then write the same row backwards underneath it.
Every column now adds to 101, and there are 100 columns: 100 × 101 = 10100.
But you wrote the list twice, so halve it: 10100 ÷ 2 = 5050.

alternativeExplanations.title: Test the trick on a tiny list
steps: A trick that works on a list you can check by hand is a trick you can trust on 100 numbers.
